summary: Page A-2 'Second Look' column by Joan Verdon, 'Writer shaped civil-rights landscape,' profiling Alfred P. Smith, a Black newspaper publisher born 1832 in Saddle River. Smith taught school, worked as a reporter for the Paterson Guardian, and in 1862 sent a letter to President Lincoln criticizing a proposal to colonize freed slaves abroad. In 1881 he began publishing A.P. Smith's Paper, renamed The Landscape, editorializing against Southern lynchings and Englewood's school segregation policy until his death in 1901 at age 69; the Hackensack Republican eulogized him as 'a conspicuous figure and a power among the men of his race.'
